summary: # 【Marvelous Designer X Crytek】Learning Day Special Guest Juefei p01 ## Introduction Hello everyone, my name is Juefei He. I am a freelancer who mainly focuses on character modeling. We are very happy to invite Juefei to the BBB official live broadcast room to conduct a special version of AMD learning. The first part will feature Juefei demonstrating how to use various 3D software to complete his work. ## Overview of the Project The work this time is a down jacket. The model is primarily done in AMD. Let's start with the character model. This is the basic body of the character I have created. ### Character Modeling The basic body model is taken from a dance studio, which provides very useful basic models that make it easier to pose characters. You can adjust the body shape according to your needs. ### Importing into Marvelous Designer (MD) After selecting a model and posing it, you can import it into MD. In MD, the system will automatically create an animation based on the pose. Initially, when creating the model, you should use either an A pose or T pose. Then, you can transform it into the desired pose. ## Material Explanation At the beginning stages, the model in MD resembles a basic A pose. A common challenge many users face is with the board shape when making custom clothing. ### Reference Pictures I use reference pictures to assist in the design and production of the board. For example, I have a U-shaped suit with a hat and jacket, with specific details referenced from the pictures. I usually find these reference pictures on platforms like Taobao, as they have a wide range of clothing shapes that are often well-designed. ## Techniques for Clothing Design When designing clothing in MD, I usually create the basic form from scratch. Most of my clothing design involves using the basic form. For more complex items like hats, I build a cap model by dragging and adjusting the shape. ### UV Mapping I utilize a software called RISMO to divide the UV. After analyzing the UV, I make cuts where necessary. I incorporate the reference picture into MD and add a background image to aid in design. ## Advanced Techniques MD has a very good function for drawing lines. If the clothing is not soundproof, you can use this feature to extract panels. When using MD, I often search online for clothing styling references to incorporate into my designs. ### Adjustments and Modifications During the modeling process, I try not to cut too thin initially. This makes adjustments easier later on. I focus on the details, such as adding creases, sewing lines, and fabric thickness in MD. ## Performance Considerations I have some performance tips regarding computer specifications. For optimal performance, especially when working with particle diameters, it's essential to use a capable computer. The effect of different diameters on performance is significant, and using a better GPU can lead to smoother calculations. ### Using CPU vs. GPU For intensive modeling tasks, I prefer to use a CPU for final calculations due to the higher accuracy compared to GPU. In the workflow, I switch between CPU and GPU based on the complexity of the model and the desired accuracy of the calculations. ## Conclusion of the Modeling Process After creating the clothing model in MD, I usually take it to ZBrush for further refinement. In ZBrush, I can simplify the model by converting it to a triangle face for easier handling. I focus on fixing any issues manually, such as connecting faces and ensuring the geometry is clean. ### Final Adjustments Once the model is refined, I check the number of faces and ensure that the final model maintains a good balance between detail and performance. After completing the necessary adjustments, I prepare the model for texturing and rendering. ## Texturing and Rendering I use Substance Painter (SP) for material creation. The process involves dragging materials from the library and adjusting them to see which works best for the model. I focus on achieving a realistic look by utilizing various effects. ### Lighting Setup In the rendering phase, I set up my lighting in a way that enhances the appearance of the fabric. I typically use a combination of main light, back light, and outline light to create depth and realism in the final render. ## Q&A Session I appreciate everyone for joining today’s session. If you have any questions, please feel free to ask.
